text:
julie_cust: Hey team — on-prem installer failing during model download and pip installs in our private VPC. Error shows an SSL issue when contacting model-registry.redwood.ai and some pip requests time out. Installer log attached (snippet below). Can someone confirm the exact egress hosts/ports we need to allow?

laura_support: Sorry you're hitting this, julie. Can you paste the exact error lines and a `curl -v` output to model-registry? Also confirm whether you have a TLS-intercepting proxy or corporate MITM that's rewriting certs.

julie_cust: Here's the relevant bits from the installer stdout:

```
ERROR: could not fetch shard https://model-registry.redwood.ai/shards/abc123 - curl exit 60
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate verify failed:
*  subjectAltName does not match
curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
pip install -r requirements.txt --timeout=60 --> connection reset
```

We don't have a full MITM normally but our corp proxy does TLS intercept for audit.

raj_engineer: That subjectAltName mismatch usually means the proxy is re-signing the cert (or SNI split-horizon). Two fast checks: 1) run `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai` from the host, paste the cert subject; 2) try `curl --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:34.120.12.45 https://model-registry.redwood.ai/shards/abc123` (replace IP with one our DNS resolves to) to see if proxy is in the middle.

julie_cust: Pasting `openssl s_client` output (trimmed):

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = DigiCert, CN = DigiCert Global Root CA
verify return:1
subject=/C=US/ST=CA/L=San Francisco/O=Redwood Inference/CN=model-registry.internal
issuer=/C=US/O=CorpIntercept/CN=Corp MITM CA
```

So it looks like our proxy is resigning with CN=model-registry.internal.

laura_support: OK that explains the cert mismatch. For the installer and runtime you need outbound HTTPS (443) to our public hostnames and DNS (UDP/TCP 53). Please request your security team to allowlist the following domains and ensure no terminating TLS proxy is doing hostname rewriting for these flows (or enable SNI passthrough):

- model-registry.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- artifacts.redwood-inference.com
- files.redwood-inference.com
- pypi.org (and pypi.python.org)
- s3.amazonaws.com (for some model artifacts)

Also allow OCSP/CRL endpoints for cert validation (usually TCP 80 outbound) and keep port 443 open to the above.

raj_engineer: Adding some CIDR suggestions you can pass to security (these are our CDN/origin ranges — allow TLS egress to these):

- 34.120.0.0/14 (example GCP block for origin)
- 52.26.0.0/16 (example AWS ELB/CDN)
- 18.205.0.0/16 (example S3 fronting)

Note: we rely on hostnames and SNI for routing; if your proxy rewrites Host/SNI you need to exempt these flows or enable passthrough.

mike_oncall: Workaround if security can't change policy quickly: pre-download the model tarball and dependency wheel files to an internal artifact repo and run installer with `--offline` plus `--package-repo http://internal-artifactory.local`. Example:

```
# on a bastion with internet access
curl -O https://files.redwood-inference.com/models/xxx.tar.gz
pip download -r requirements.txt -d /tmp/wheels
# then point installer at local artifacts
./installer.sh --offline --local-model /tmp/xxx.tar.gz --pip-wheel-dir /tmp/wheels
```

laura_support: Also note telemetry will attempt to reach telemetry.redwood.ai over outbound 443; you can disable telemetry during install with `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0 ./installer.sh` if you want to expedite. But long-term we recommend allowing the domains so automatic updates and health metrics work.

julie_cust: I filed a request with security asking to allow SNI passthrough for the domains and to exempt the installer IP range. They asked for a short justification — what should I put?

laura_support: Paste: "Redwood Inference on-prem installer and runtime require egress to listed hostnames for model registry, artifact storage, auth, and telemetry. TLS passthrough is required to preserve certificate validation (SNI must not be terminated). Blocking or re-signing TLS breaks certificate subjectAltName and causes installer failures and runtime auth errors." Add the domain list from above.

eng-infra-bot: NOTE: If using a split-horizon DNS or private resolver, ensure private A records for the above hostnames are resolvable from the installer host and that DNS does not point to internal proxies that re-terminate TLS.

raj_engineer: If you can share a short firewall flow log sample (src ip, dst ip, dst port, action) for a failed attempt we can correlate on our side. Also include the output of `nslookup model-registry.redwood.ai` from the host.

julie_cust: Will send logs. Quick update — security approved passthrough for the domains and disabled TLS intercept for the installer host. Re-ran installer with telemetry disabled and it completed. Thanks!

laura_support: Great — can you confirm final state? Also we'll follow up with a KB article for on-prem allowlist and a permanent list for the ALLOWLIST ticket.

julie_cust: Confirmed: installer completed, model loaded, agent running. Please open a permanent allowlist change with our security team referencing this thread (I'll share ticket id). Thanks! :tada:
